## Theorem III (positive *rational* equilibria of detailed-balanced reaction networks are decidable)

Let a finite mass-action chemical reaction network consist of reversible reaction pairs `alpha_j <-> beta_j`, with integer nonnegative complexes and **positive rational** forward/backward rate constants `k_j^+, k_j^-`. Suppose it is known (or promised) that it is **detailed-balanced**, i.e. there exists at least one real positive concentration vector `x_*` satisfying equality of both reaction fluxes of every pair.

Then there is a terminating exact algorithm deciding whether the system has **any** strictly positive rational-coordinate equilibrium. When one exists, the algorithm constructs one. Without the detailed-balance promise, the algorithm still decides existence of a positive **rational detailed-balanced** state, but not the existence of arbitrary rational stationary states.

### Proof (global, not a specified stoichiometric compatibility class)

For each pair let `B_j=beta_j-alpha_j` be an integer row vector and `c_j=k_j^+/k_j^->0`. The detailed-balance equations are exactly

    product_i x_i^{B_{j,i}} = c_j   (j=1,...,m).

Factor all finitely many positive rational `c_j` into rational primes, let `P` be their finite set of divisors. For each prime p in P form the integer column `b_p=(v_p(c_j))_j`, and solve the **integer linear system**

    B n_p = b_p,    n_p in Z^d.

Integer solvability is decidable by Smith normal form. If one system is inconsistent, there is no positive rational solution. If all are solvable, put

    x_i = product_{p in P} p^{(n_p)_i}  in Q_{>0}.

For every reaction j, the valuations at all primes p of `x^{B_j}` and `c_j` coincide (both have zero valuations outside P), so `x^{B_j}=c_j` exactly. Conversely any rational detailed-balanced x yields integer solutions `n_p=(v_p(x_i))_i` for every p in P. Hence this algorithm is exact and constructive. (The empty P case yields x_i=1, if all c_j=1.)

    F(x)=sum_i [x_i log(x_i/x_{*,i})-x_i+x_{*,i}].

Its derivative along mass-action dynamics is

    dF/dt = -sum_j (f_j(x)-r_j(x)) log[f_j(x)/r_j(x)] <= 0,

## Exact flow and kinetic realizability

Take

    M(x,y)=(x-y)^2 >=0,
    dx/dt=M(x,y)(1-x),
    dy/dt=M(x,y)(1-y).

These are polynomial ODEs on (0,infty)^2. Both coordinates are monotone toward 1, so every positive orbit remains in a compact positive rectangle and converges to an equilibrium. The potential `V=((x-1)^2+(y-1)^2)/2` is globally 1-strongly convex and satisfies `dV/dt=-M||grad V||²`. The equilibrium set contains the entire positive diagonal x=y, and (1,1) is the unique minimum of V.

Expanded:

    F_x = -x³+2x²y+x²-xy²-2xy+y².
    F_y = -x²y+x²+2xy²-2xy-y³+y².

This flow **does** have an ordinary kinetic mass-action realization: for each positive coefficient `+k x^alpha` in coordinate i, use a reaction `alpha -> alpha+e_i` of rate k; for each negative coefficient `-k x^alpha` use `alpha -> alpha-e_i` of rate k. Every negative monomial in F_i contains its consumed species, so all target complexes are nonnegative. This realizes the polynomial vector field exactly, although the resulting network need not be reversible.

## No weakly reversible dynamically equivalent network (without auxiliaries)

**Lemma (maximal-source direction).** Let a finite polynomial vector field F be realized by a weakly reversible mass-action network. For any linear functional w on the exponent/source space and any monomial support exponent alpha of F whose w-weight is **maximal among all monomials with nonzero vector-field coefficient**, it is impossible that `w dot [x^alpha]F >0`. Here `[x^alpha]F` is the coefficient vector of that monomial.

**Proof.** Consider a weakly reversible component containing the source alpha. Let h be the maximum w-weight of its complexes. If h exceeded the maximum weight H of the nonzero-coefficient support of F, then some source on the h-maximal face must have an outgoing edge to smaller weight (a directed return path from any lower complex to this component ensures such an edge in a strongly connected component). Its net w-drift would be strictly negative, because every outgoing edge from a maximizer has nonpositive w-projection. But F has no monomial coefficient at weight h>H. Contradiction. Thus no component producing the coefficient at alpha can contain a source of weight exceeding H; consequently the w-projection of its contribution at alpha (weight H) is <=0.
